races.name: Blink And You Miss It Sprint Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, Solar Acclaim returns after 63 days and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid grounding for conditions; his ninth last time out tempers expectations, but at 136 lb from stall four, his overall profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Exclamation
runners_data.note: Grace Harris three-year-old with a good Goodwood 5f win to his name but all five recent runs came on good or faster ground — soft is unproven and may blunt his prominent-racing speed; Oisin Orr booking is an upgrade.
runners_data.comment: Exclamation has distance and going experience in his favour, and a second two starts back gives him a recent placed effort to build on; however, unplaced runs either side of that and a ranking of sixth of ten suggest he faces a stiff task under 135 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Cinque Verde
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner; Tony Carroll handler with a modest 14-day strike rate but this horse dictates entirely on his own terms from stall, and one soft-ground win from just one similar-going start suggests he handles the conditions; pace dynamics are strongly in his favour.

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse most comfortable off the pace, with soft-going experience (4th over 5f soft most recently); Geoffrey Harker yard quiet at 0/5 and the 8-day turnaround is brisk, though he does show a placed effort on soft at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Sir Yoshi shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here just eight days later in fine freshness, with experience over today's trip and going adding to his claims; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and a tough weight of 132 lb from stall eight may test his resolution.

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Two soft-ground wins in his last five (1st and 1st over 5f soft), making him one of the best-credentialled horses in the field for today's conditions; PJ McDonald in the saddle and the tongue-strap likely helps him settle — naturally a hold-up type but with soft-going class to close from midfield.
runners_data.comment: Trilby won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, but his last two outings have brought a defeat and a fourth, suggesting he may be just off the boil; 130 lb is no easy burden from stall three.

runners_data.name: Paddy's Day
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a solid placed record but all recent runs on good or standard ground — going suitability is the key question mark; Alex Jary's 3lb claim helps on the weights and Nigel Tinkler's yard has been quiet at 0/21 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Paddy's Day arrives 57 days fresh and yet to win in his last six starts, though a third last time out and a second three starts back hint at ability; a trainer in poor current form — zero from 21 over the past fortnight — is the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Temple Of Athena
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison three-year-old who showed early promise (two wins from 13 similar-going runs) but has produced a string of mid-pack finishes recently; 54 days off and no soft-ground runs in the recent record make this a speculative prominent entry.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Temple Of Athena has been stuck in the minors in her last five starts, with a win six starts back her only recent bright spot, and a trainer firing at just 5% over the past fortnight makes it hard to get enthusiastic despite experience over today's trip and distance.

runners_data.name: Francisco's Piece
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good going and has five soft-going runs in recent history (0W, 3P) suggesting he handles it; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural closer's role is compressed by the volume of hold-up types in this field, slightly reducing the chance he gets the clean late run he ideally needs.
runners_data.comment: Francisco's Piece arrives here in form, winning last time out and earning a rating of 90 that marks him out as one to beat from stall nine, carrying 128 lb; the chief concern is whether he can back that up after a 29-day absence.

runners_data.name: Lethal Nymph
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's veteran has placed on soft before and won over 5f on standard last time; racing 9 days after that run is tight, and as a natural hold-up horse he at least sits in his genuine role — soft ground helps his finishing kick if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lethal Nymph is hard to fancy despite an encouraging win last time out; he has experience of today's trip and going, but his overall recent form is patchy and he represents a stiff ask from this position in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey runner with two soft-ground placed efforts in recent history and a very recent 13-day return; a genuine back-of-the-field type whose finishing run is squeezed by the number of closers in this race, though the soft ground and fitness angle give him an outside claims.
runners_data.comment: Vintage Clarets catches the eye on our rating, topping the field of ten, and he arrives fit on a 13-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, carrying 127 lb from stall two; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, though a third three starts back hints at residual ability.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's eight-year-old has soft-going placed form over 6f but all recent outings have been on good or standard; a natural hold-up horse whose chance is further tempered by being pushed into a midfield role he cannot fully exploit, and the blinkered runner has never won on soft.
runners_data.comment: Baldomero is winless in his last six starts and ranks ninth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy here; a third three starts back offers slim encouragement, but back-to-back disappointing runs since leave him with plenty to prove carrying 126 lb from stall 11.

races.paceDynamic: Cinque Verde is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, Connor Beasley can control tempo from the gates and set whatever fractions suit — on soft ground at Beverley's tight 5f, that is likely to mean a strongly-run but metronomically even gallop rather than an suicidal burn. Solar Acclaim, Exclamation, Paddy's Day and Temple Of Athena will all want to race prominently, creating a competitive early order behind the leader but no single horse likely to hunt Cinque Verde down from the front. Francisco's Piece, Vintage Clarets and Baldomero are natural hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield picture on the map because there are more closers in this field than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — of those three, Vintage Clarets (soft-ground form, recent run) and Lethal Nymph are best placed to find legitimate cover and deliver late. The soft ground slows sectionals and stretches the advantage of a controlled lead, meaning prominent racers who can track Cinque Verde without overdoing it early — rather than deep closers forced wide and late — are the profile this race shape favours most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cinque Verde Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cinque Verde is allowed to stride clear from the gates with no rival willing to match him through the early stages on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Beasley dictates a sustainable but punishing pace on the testing surface and the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up in 5f at Beverley; the leader's relaxed rhythm means his reserves are intact for the final furlong climb.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up-style horses placed prominently tracks Cinque Verde throughout and outstays him in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: The soft ground rewards horses who travel smoothly in behind the pace without expending energy early; a prominent tracker who settles sweetly can exploit any late leg-weary moment from the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stops Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground proves more taxing than expected and Cinque Verde ties up inside the final furlong, gifting closers a window.
scenarios.body: Lethal Nymph and Vintage Clarets, both with soft-ground form, would be the natural beneficiaries, though both are operating at least partially out of their deepest preferred hold-up role given the field makeup.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If early positions are contested more fiercely than expected and the whole field converges in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An unusually compressed finish would hand an each-way chance to Sir Yoshi or Baldomero finding daylight late, though both have limited soft-ground form and are working against the dominant race shape.

watchPoints.text: Cinque Verde — if he jumps cleanly from the gates and is immediately allowed to stride clear without a challenger, his lone-leader status on soft ground makes him extremely difficult to peg back in the final furlong.

Trilby — PJ McDonald has soft-ground winning form on this horse and will be hunting the leader from midfield; watch how quickly he picks up once straightened, as two soft 5f wins mark him as the most likely beneficiary if Cinque Verde weakens.

Lethal Nymph — a 9-day turnaround after a win is quick but Paul Midgley does run horses back fast; if the field fans out in the straight, he is the deepest closer with a genuine profile for the ground.

Exclamation — all five recent runs are on good or faster ground; watch in the market to see if connections are confident on soft, because a going concern could see him over-bet relative to his actual suitability.

Francisco's Piece, Vintage Clarets, Baldomero — the three redistributed hold-up types: watch their early positioning to see if any manages to find genuine cover at the rear; if all are forced wider and into midfield traffic, their chances diminish further from an already compromised starting point.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: L'Eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner who has placed four times in six recent starts at 1m2f on good, and the step up to 1m4f on soft is an unknown; a genuine hold-up horse in practice whose style means he needs plenty to go wrong ahead to collect, and the overcrowded rear of this field complicates matters further.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer who has finished third three times in his last four starts, L'Eagle Aid arrives fresh on 27 days' rest, has run over today's trip, and our rating puts him ahead of his official mark — yet to win in recent starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's front-runner returns after 63 days off with two Southwell wins from the front this year, but soft turf is a different proposition and his lone soft outing in the data yielded no placing; the key question is whether fitness holds for the full 1m4f after a two-month absence.
runners_data.comment: Clansman boasts a winner two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with his rating of 76 giving him a solid claims; the chief concern is that unplaced effort last time out after a 63-day break that stretches into this return.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Samantha & Jacqueline Coward's eight-year-old has a win and two places at 1m2f-2m on good ground but none of her recent form reads well on soft; she is a true hold-up horse by inclination, and in a field stacked with similar types she faces a traffic and positional puzzle before she can even deliver her effort.
runners_data.comment: Valley of Flowers has won in recent starts but sits eighth of nine on our figures, making her hard to fancy at the weights with 137 lb to carry; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a run 36 days ago leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Calypso
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old carries headgear and is lightly raced over staying trips, with a recent Southwell win at 1m2f suggesting he handles varying surfaces; Oisin Orr takes over and, critically, he has shown enough tactical flexibility to race closer than his natural position, making him well-suited if Clansman sets a conservative pace.
runners_data.comment: Prince Of Calypso won last time out and returns just 12 days later in fine fettle, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour; a rating of 78 underlines his claims, and he is our pick to go in again.

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's juvenile has a win at 1m2f on good ground and a second at 9f, so the step to 1m4f on soft is an unproven combination; Tom Eaves rides and the 49-day absence is worth monitoring, but if he settles midfield and the ground doesn't inconvenience, he has the engine to compete.
runners_data.comment: Mayaada shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip, while her rating of 79 makes her the one to beat here; the concern is a fourth last time out after 49 days off.

runners_data.name: Northern Brave
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' three-year-old won over 8f at Haydock on heavy, so soft ground is not a concern; however, his natural hold-up style is compromised by the glut of closers in this field, and Connor Beasley will struggle to find a clean passage from a rear position in a single-file soft-ground contest.
runners_data.comment: Northern Brave shaped well last time, finishing second, though a fourth two starts back and a seventh three starts back hint at inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and returns after 28 days, carrying 132 lb on an official mark of 74.

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old won over 9f on soft at Haydock, giving him the strongest soft-ground credentials in the field for a closer; David Nolan partners and, crucially, his style allows him to race with enough positional awareness to slot just off the pace — making him the hold-up horse best equipped to exploit an uncontested Clansman.
runners_data.comment: Unchartedterritory was a winner two starts back but ran flat last time, and that sixth leaves him needing to bounce back here; no distance or going experience is noted, though he arrives on a reasonable freshener of 21 days and our rating gives him a fighting chance in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Barak Warrior
runners_data.note: James Keane's three-year-old won over 1m4f on firm at Hamilton, so the distance is proven but soft ground and a significant weight reduction are both relevant factors; P J McDonald rides and while there's raw ability here, the horse's hold-up profile leaves him dependent on a pace scenario that this race is unlikely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Barak Warrior's recent form is patchy, with two sevenths and an eighth in his last five starts offsetting that win two starts back, and our figures rank him seventh of nine here, making him hard to fancy despite the distance experience and a third last time out.

runners_data.name: Topathemorning
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' three-year-old has never won beyond 6f and all four starts are at shorter distances, making this 1m4f on soft a significant step into the unknown; Ethan Tindall (5lb claimer) rides, and with no soft-ground form and a raw form line of 6-588, this runner looks outgunned by class and stamina requirements alike.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with back-to-back eighths making her hard to fancy from the bottom of our rankings, Topathemorning at least returns reasonably fresh on 33 days off and carries a workable 120lb.

races.paceDynamic: Clansman is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, will slot onto the lead from stall and set whatever tempo he chooses over this 1m4f on soft ground at Beverley — a track that naturally tests stamina through its long home straight. His recent Southwell form shows two wins from front-running, and with no horse in this field equipped or positioned to pressurise him early, the pace is likely to be controlled and measured rather than searching. That moderate, single-file tempo on soft ground will suit those who can travel close to the action and pounce in the straight, rather than those forced to produce runs from far back. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — L'Eagle Aid, Valley Of Flowers, Northern Brave, Barak Warrior, and Topathemorning are all genuine closers who will be competing for the same ground; those able to slot closer to the pace than their natural style dictates — Unchartedterritory and Prince Of Calypso, who have shown versatility — are best positioned to exploit a steadily-run affair, while true deep closers face a harder task when the gallop is unlikely to be genuinely strong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clansman Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman leads at his own pace and the soft ground blunts any late challenges from hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Clansman controls a moderate tempo throughout, and the long Beverley straight simply emphasises stamina over finishing speed, rewarding horses who have tracked closely rather than come from off the pace; with so many genuine closers unable to produce their full finishing kick in the ground, the prominent tracker who stays on wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned second or third early picks off a tiring Clansman inside the final furlong on the soft surface.
scenarios.body: Clansman's layoff of 63 days and advancing age (8) raises fitness questions, and if he fades in the closing stages a well-placed stalker inherits the race without needing a big late surge; this shape rewards horses with enough tactical speed to travel prominently without burning energy early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and the closing stages become an extended stamina test in deep ground.
scenarios.body: A truly crawling gallop followed by a messy final two furlongs could see a genuine stayer grind through the mud rather than accelerate; horses with soft-ground form and a proven stamina base over this trip or further hold the edge, though most in this field have done their winning on a faster surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman sets an unexpectedly strong gallop that burns runners out, opening the door for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types finding space and momentum from the rear, which is structurally unlikely given how many true closers are competing for the same wide path; even if the pace quickens, soft ground on a flat track punishes horses who must cover extra ground late.

watchPoints.text: Clansman's fitness after 63 days off is the central variable — if he ties up early in the straight, every scenario shifts dramatically and Prince Of Calypso or Unchartedterritory inherit the contest.

The cluster of six genuine hold-up horses competing for the same rear positions risks interference and traffic issues rounding the bend into the straight — watch Barak Warrior and Northern Brave in particular for being denied a clear run.

Valley Of Flowers has zero soft-ground wins and a style that is difficult to deploy when surrounded by horses of identical inclination — monitor whether Joanna Mason is forced into an uncharacteristic positional decision early.

Unchartedterritory's soft-ground win at Haydock over 9f is the standout going-specific credential among the hold-up contingent — watch whether David Nolan pushes forward earlier than expected to exploit that advantage.
Topathemorning represents a significant step up in trip and class and has no form on soft — watch the betting for any drifts that confirm market scepticism about this runner's suitability on the day.

races.name: Dearing Plastics Celebrating 40 Years Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sands
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up operator with winning form over 10f on good, but the sim-going record reads 0W 0P from 15 attempts on similar ground, which is a significant concern on today's soft surface; Joanna Mason takes the ride for the Easterbys but the conditions expose this runner's limitations.
runners_data.comment: Shimmering Sands won back-to-back races earlier in this sequence and ran third last time out to advertise solid current form, and with distance experience and a 22-day break leaving him fresh, the main query is whether 142 lb will anchor his chance from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Project Geofin
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald booked for a hold-up type who has finished no better than third in recent starts and whose sim-going record is equally poor (0W 0P from 15 runs); without a strong gallop to close into, the tactical setup actively works against this runner's chance.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a second five starts back, Project Geofin returns on a quick 14-day turnaround having run over today's trip before, and his rating of 82 marks him as the one to beat from stall 11 off 142 lb, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter whose recent form shows a win at this trip on good ground; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that it has been mapped as a prominent runner now being asked to lead, but it is the only horse in the field who will actually dictate, which gives it inherent positional value regardless of that caveat.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a placed effort three starts back, bringing solid recent form and distance experience to the table; the risk is that a fourth last time out shows he does not always fire, and 142 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a sharp profile — three wins from five runs including a win on soft at 8f — and OR 73 represents competitive claims at this level; Oisin Orr is a high-calibre booking and, as a genuine prominent type who can stalk from second or third, the race shape is made for this runner.
runners_data.comment: Ciao Capo won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid claims, though a sixth two starts back interrupts the sequence and 133 lb is no featherweight ask from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Rapide Vega
runners_data.note: Won last time at 8f on standard and has placed twice on soft in five runs; at OR 73 with recent winning form and the ability to race prominently, M.P. Sheehy's mount looks well-placed to challenge if tracking the leader without interference from the compressed midfield.
runners_data.comment: Rapide Vega won last time out and returns fit on just 12 days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going; at 133 lb from stall one, the weight is the one factor worth watching.

runners_data.name: Musical Accord
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett-trained three-year-old returning from an 86-day break with just three runs to show, all in midfield or rear, on good-to-soft or standard ground; the absence, lack of soft-ground experience and hold-up profile all point away from this race shape suiting.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Musical Accord faces a stiff ask returning from 86 days off, though she has run over today's trip and a spot of freshness can occasionally spark improvement.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has a win and a third on soft in four runs on similar going (0W 1P), so the conditions are not a worry; Connor Beasley keeps the ride and, racing prominently, Ziata maps into a position where she could challenge from mid-pack if the pace is truly moderate.
runners_data.comment: Ziata showed she can win, landing the spoils two starts back, though she comes here on the back of an unplaced effort and faces a stiff task ranked sixth of eleven; she has run over today's trip and going, and 129 lb from stall four is the reality she must overcome.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's runner has two wins on soft over shorter trips and genuine prominent-racing credentials — but the redistribution reflects that too many horses want that position, and with a STYLE_FIT flag, it may not get the clean early berth its recent form was built on.
runners_data.comment: Fans Favourite arrives here on the back of a third last time out, and a winner three starts back, giving him a mixed profile to weigh up; experience over today's trip and going helps, though carrying 128 lb from stall six on a our rating of 73 makes this no gimme.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent six-year-old holds solid recent form (five placings from six runs) and is a hold-up type at heart whose redistribution into midfield signals it is racing outside its ideal shape; without a proper gallop to chase, closing runs from this position rarely materialise at Beverley.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sunny Orange ranks tenth of eleven on our figures and looks hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a fresh 14-day break carrying 126 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Distinction
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer carrying a visor and a STYLE_FIT flag; an 8-year-old whose sim-going record shows 1W 2P from 15 attempts is not terrible, but the redistribution away from its natural trailing position and John Mackie's quiet 14-day record (0/4) dampen expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with just one placed effort in that sequence, Distinction is hard to fancy on these figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; the 23-day break offers little consolation.

runners_data.name: Lady Hornblower
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's three-year-old has placed on soft over 8f but recent form figures of 9-8-6-3-7 show inconsistency, and the redistribution from its natural prominent position into a midfield mapping with a 0.94 STYLE_FIT flag means it is unlikely to get the racing room its best efforts have required.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Hornblower at least showed some promise with a third two runs back, though her most recent seventh suggests she remains inconsistent; she has run over today's distance and going before, but a mark of 62 and draw two leave her with plenty to find under 122 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Everyoneknowsadave is the confirmed sole front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine pressure expected to emerge from the gate, is set to dictate a controlled, measured gallop over this 1m2f on soft ground at Beverley. The redistribution flags confirm the field is loaded with prominent and hold-up types — Fans Favourite, Lady Hornblower, Sunny Orange and Distinction are all natural pace-seeking or hold-up horses who will struggle to get their preferred position and will be shuffled into a midfield cluster, creating a compressed, tactical race behind the leader. On soft going at Beverley, which is an undulating, sharp-turning track that rewards horses who travel economically and have a turn of foot rather than sheer staying power, a race run at a sustainable clip by one lone leader sets up ideally for prominent-to-midfield horses who can settle close enough to the pace and produce a clean, well-timed challenge entering the home straight. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who can genuinely stalk the front-runner from second or third place, travel within themselves, and pick up in the straight are most favoured — true hold-up types relying on a strong gallop to close into are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave bowls along uncontested and sets a soft, controlled tempo that dries up the late kick of hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: The sole front-runner dictates every yard at a pace that suits its own stamina on soft ground, and horses tracking from second or third — Ciao Capo, Rapide Vega — are ideally placed to pick up the pieces if the leader tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Sweep Past
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave sets just enough pace that a well-placed tracker can cruise into contention and assert from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Ciao Capo and Rapide Vega, both genuine prominent types with winning form and course/distance profile, settle in behind the leader and produce a sustained challenge that the lone front-runner cannot repel on the soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses late and the compressed midfield group produces an unexpected finisher with reserves.
scenarios.body: Shimmering Sands or Musical Accord, racing from further back, could benefit if the ground tests stamina more than anticipated and the front horses are all spent; however, the soft going and lack of strong pace makes a true late swoop structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave is considerably better than its OR suggests and simply gallops rivals into the ground on the soft.
scenarios.body: A race run at a falsely slow early pace can paradoxically become a true test in the closing stages on soft ground, and a horse with tactical speed plus stamina reserves could win more comfortably than the market expects.

watchPoints.text: Ciao Capo has three wins in five starts including a soft-ground success, is a genuine prominent type who maps perfectly to stalk Everyoneknowsadave, and Oisin Orr is a significant jockey upgrade — watch for this runner to travel powerfully into contention from the home turn.

Everyoneknowsadave is the only confirmed front-runner but is flagged as racing slightly out of role as a prominent type forced to lead; if it misses the break or is taken on unexpectedly, the race loses its shape entirely and the pace dynamic collapses.

The midfield cluster is artificially compressed by multiple redistributed prominent types — Fans Favourite, Lady Hornblower and Ziata — which creates a real risk of traffic problems and interference on the home turn at Beverley where the track narrows significantly.

Soft ground is uniform across the card at Beverley today and no runner stands out with strong sim-going form — Shimmering Sands and Project Geofin both carry 0W 0P records from 15 similar-going runs, which makes them vulnerable in these conditions despite competitive ORs.

Rapide Vega won last time and has placed on soft, but the step up to 1m2f from 8f and 10f dominates its recent form history — watch whether it relaxes early enough to see out the trip under today's conditions.

races.name: IRE-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Churchill Tyres Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for David O'Meara who has been running in soft recently (5th over 7f soft last time); the sim-going record is uninspiring at 1W from 15 and the hold-up style is a real concern in a race where the pace is likely to be honest rather than suicidal — needs things to go perfectly late.|
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has run over today's trip and returns on a sharp ten-day turnaround in fine fettle, his rating of 85 suggesting he merits more respect than his official mark of 78 implies; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and breaking that duck from stall one is the challenge.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this David Loughnane-trained 4yo who has won twice recently including a course win; the prominent style and recent form (461121) are compelling, though the sim-going record is just 2 runs with no wins — the step back to soft is the key variable to resolve.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, The Sweet Escape makes this a tough assignment despite a lively recent sequence of three wins in his last six starts; he has run over today's trip and returns on a sound 15-day break, but the weight of 136 lb from stall 13 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for the Barron yard who races prominently from the off; the 0/7 trainer 14-day stat is a flag, and Swift Salian has placed twice on soft but never won on the surface — will likely push Mudamer for the lead and the question is whether either can last.|
runners_data.comment: Swift Salian has been a model of consistency in placing, with three seconds in his last five starts, though he remains yet to win and an unplaced run last time out is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough to threaten again.

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: John & Sean Quinn's 4yo is a hold-up type who won on soft (1/8f/SOF) and has form figures to respect; the 35-day absence and moderate sim-going record (1W from 9) are mild concerns, but the soft ground win is a genuine positive in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Zowal has a win three starts back and was third two starts back, but an unplaced effort last time and a ranking of tenth of twelve on our figures make him hard to fancy; he has run over today's trip and 35 days off shouldn't inconvenience him.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends out this 6yo with Connor Beasley, who is expert around Beverley; the prominent style, recent win (1/8f/GOO), and trainer's strong 14-day form (4/25) make this an attractive profile — the absence of soft-ground wins is noted but the horse's consistency in placing suggests it handles cut.|
runners_data.comment: Glenfinnan won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but an unplaced effort two starts back and 142 lb from stall 10 are factors to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 6yo has a fade-in-finish flag attached to its profile which is a significant concern in a true-run race on soft ground that will test stamina throughout; the form figures (015504) show no recent wins and the lack of soft-ground form in the history compounds the doubt.|

runners_data.name: Mudamer
runners_data.note: Geoffrey Harker's 7yo is one of the two confirmed front-runners and sets the pace dynamic for the whole race; the 45-day absence is noted, the sim-going record is only 2/15 with one win, and everything depends on whether the strong early gallop it creates leaves enough in reserve for the uphill Beverley finish.|
runners_data.comment: Mudamer has placed three times in his last five starts, including third last time out, and has run over today's distance and going before, making him a genuine threat from stall two on a mark of 80; the concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo with David Allan is a prominent type with a soft-ground second in recent history (2/7f/SOF); the trainer's prolific 14-day record (5/86) is noise rather than signal, but the prominent style and distance profile suit the likely race shape well.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out on suitable distance and going, Son heads this 12-runner field as the top-rated contender on an 87 rating, and a return to form after a flat run two starts back looks on the cards; yet to win in recent starts, he nevertheless appeals as the one to beat under 139 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: One Night Thunder
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 6yo with the 5lb claimer Whiteley holds soft-ground form (8th over 8f soft) and is a hold-up horse whose style will be compressed by the number of rear-dwellers in this field; the OR of 73 is competitive but the horse needs everything to fall right to make an impact.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, One Night Thunder does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return to form showed with a third four starts back; however, recent efforts of sixth, seventh and eighth suggest he faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's 3yo is stepping up slightly in trip after a close second at 6f on good ground; the prominent style suits the likely shape but the horse has no soft-ground experience in its history, which is a genuine unknown — the 31-day break and youth of the trainer record (0/3 in 14 days) are worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Arduis Invicta nonetheless shaped with promise when second three starts back, and our rating of 86 marks her as a serious contender here; the risk is that unplaced efforts last time out and six starts back raise a question over consistency.

runners_data.name: Highland Shah
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 3yo showed placed form recently (3/7f/GOO) and has a low OR of 71 to exploit; no soft-ground win in the history but consistent placed form — the prominent style means it can be covered up behind the pace battle and delivered, though the 51-day absence is the longest in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Highland Shah returns after 51 days off and, ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, is hard to fancy at these weights, though he does bring a win two starts back and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 3yo is a genuine hold-up horse by nature whose true rearward position has been compressed onto the midfield map by the volume of hold-up types in this race; the recent form includes soft-ground placed efforts and the 3lb claim is useful, but racing closer to the pace than preferred means its true chance is harder to land.|
runners_data.comment: Shadow Run has shown consistency without converting, with a second two starts back and fifth last time out, but he remains winless in recent starts and his trainer is in a difficult patch of form at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 3yo has strong placed form (four places in last five including on soft) and is a natural hold-up racer who finds itself mapped to midfield because the field cannot accommodate all rear-dwellers at the back; the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence, though the consistent soft-ground placed form is the most genuine positive in the horse's favour.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Supreme Clarets faces a stiff ask, though he arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving connections something to build on.

races.paceDynamic: Mudamer and Swift Salian are the confirmed front-runners in this 13-runner field, and on soft ground over 7½f at Beverley they will set an honest, pressured gallop from the outset — neither is the type to roll over and concede the lead without a fight. The early battle between these two will ensure the pace is genuine rather than processed, which on soft turf over this trip historically stretches the field and makes it very difficult for true hold-up horses to make up ground from the back. Glenfinnan, The Sweet Escape, Son, and Arduis Invicta are the prominent types best placed to track the pace at a comfortable distance and pounce once the front-runners feel the ground — this shape squarely favours prominent racers who can sit second or third and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp turn of foot. Shadow Run and Supreme Clarets are genuine hold-up horses in nature but have been displaced to midfield on the map because this field carries more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their preferred rear position; of the true front-runners, Mudamer is marginally more likely to control the rail and dictate terms, with Swift Salian likely to press alongside.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested pace, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mudamer and Swift Salian fight for the lead and set a genuinely strong gallop on the soft, the race sets up for a prominent tracker to mow them down.
scenarios.body: The sustained early pace burns off the front-runners in the final two furlongs on tiring ground, allowing a horse who has sat two or three lengths off the pace to hit the line with the most left in the tank; Beverley's uphill finish on soft rewards those who conserve energy through the race before unleashing a relentless gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner dictates and holds
scenarios.trigger: If Mudamer settles into a comfortable rhythm and Swift Salian drops away early, allowing a controlled rather than contested lead.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner able to dictate its own fractions on soft ground can slow the tempo just enough in the middle of the race to preserve energy for the climb home; on a course where leaders who control pace can hold on, Mudamer's course familiarity and honest front-running style give it a genuine chance of lasting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses spring surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or is slower than expected and the field bunches, giving hold-up types a realistic chance of finishing through.
scenarios.body: Misunderstood and Zowal, who prefer to come from off the pace, would need a target to aim at and a relatively short run to the line — the soft ground does compress the pace somewhat and Beverley's undulations can create pockets; however, Shadow Run and Supreme Clarets are mapped out of their true rearward position, meaning the genuine closers are fewer than they appear and this scenario depends heavily on Misunderstood and Zowal producing a rare best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft ground attrition scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the ground is more testing than Soft and the pace proves so brutal that multiple horses capitulate, turning the finish into a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: In a true stamina test the race can be won by a horse who simply stays on strongest through the mud rather than one with tactical speed; Highland Shah's proven stamina profile on similar ground and Supreme Clarets' consistent placed form on soft-side surfaces make them candidates for a late plod-through finish if the pace destroys the field.

watchPoints.text: Mudamer and Swift Salian will fight for the lead from stalls to the first bend — watch for either horse being carried wide or losing position, as the outcome of that battle will dictate the entire race shape.

Shadow Run and Supreme Clarets are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield on the race map — if neither can drop back to their natural position in running, their chance is materially reduced and any forecast built around a late flourish from them should be treated with caution.

Obelix carries a confirmed fade-in-finish flag and the soft ground over 7½f at Beverley will stretch its stamina to the limit — watch for it dropping out tamely from the two-furlong pole if the pace has been genuine.

Highland Shah is the longest absentee in the field at 51 days — monitor market moves late as Julie Camacho will have had a specific reason to wait this long, and any significant support could indicate the horse is ready to run to its best after the break.

The 7½f Beverley trip on soft going consistently produces a strong-staying winner who has tracked the pace — keep an eye on Glenfinnan's position in the first two furlongs, as a clean jump and early berth just off the leaders would put it in the ideal spot throughout.

races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week 2026 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has won over seven furlongs on soft ground, making this step up to mile-and-a-half on soft a stiff stamina test; she will set the pace but her ability to see out the extra distance is the key question, and connections have not run her beyond nine furlongs previously.
runners_data.comment: Glorious Kitty landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and a runner-up finish two starts back underlines her consistency at this level; the main concern is that sixth last time out leaves her needing to bounce back after 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer fitted with a hood and tongue tie, with one win from two soft-ground starts in his last fifteen runs; Shane Gray rides and Sam England's yard is in quiet form at T14 (0/4), but he stays the trip and should be ideally positioned just off the early duel.
runners_data.comment: Coolree has shown some ability — third two starts back and runner-up on a couple of occasions in recent starts — yet has gone winless in his last six, and a seventh last time out after 34 days raises a fitness query; he has distance and going experience to call on, but looks to have it all to do from eighth in the draw.

runners_data.name: Borjina
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old hold-up filly, whose trainer is in strong current form (7/29 T14); she won over seven furlongs on good ground and this soft mile-and-a-half is a step into unknown territory for her, though Kevin Stott's patient judgment could extract maximum value from the contested pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 10 of 12 on our figures, Borjina is hard to fancy at the weights, though she does return from a 31-day break in reasonable order and has run over today's trip before; a second two starts back is her only recent encouragement, with a fifth last time out and a seventh three starts back making the overall profile uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Promising three-year-old for David O'Meara who has won on good ground over seven furlongs and placed twice over a mile; has no soft-ground form to point to, but his claim-ridden pilot Conor Whiteley takes 5lb off and his prominent style maps perfectly to this pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Placed in three of her last four starts, including a second two runs back and third last time out, Sandy Craic arrives here in fine recent nick after 21 days off and has run over today's trip before; the main risk is whether her rating of 71 can quite match the demands at the top of the weights carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Good Morning Alex
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer who has been off 101 days and finished no better than fifth in his last six runs; his soft-going record is respectable (1W2P from five runs) but a lengthy absence and ordinary recent form make him a hard horse to trust at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 101 days off, Good Morning Alex faces questions about fitness, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a fifth two starts back offers a modest crumb of encouragement from an otherwise disappointing recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Regalian
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fitted with a hood who was beaten out of sight in eight of his last ten starts and ran only seven days ago; Tony Coyle and Kaine Wood's charge has zero wins or places from twelve attempts at similar going, making him very hard to recommend from any angle.
runners_data.comment: Regalian is winless in his last five starts but rates well clear of his rivals on our figures, and with experience over today's trip and going already banked, he arrives fit just seven days on from his latest outing carrying 140 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner fitted with tongue tie and hood who ran here over a mile on good ground last time (fifth of six) and is stepping up sharply in trip; Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim helps the weight, but the horse's recent form reads two zeros and this soft ground and extra distance add further doubt.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old prominent racer who carries a hood and has placed twice from five starts; the yard is in good form (5/39 T14) and Jason Hart is an experienced pilot, but Glen Nevis has no soft-ground experience and has been placed mainly over a mile on good ground.
runners_data.comment: Glen Nevis has been remarkably consistent in recent starts, finishing second twice and third once in his last six, and returning fresh on just nine days' rest having run over today's trip before; the risk is he remains yet to win in that same sequence.

runners_data.name: Tarmonbarry Kid
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up performer with a soft-ground win (1/8f/SOF) to his name, representing the Fahey yard who send runners to win; 73 days off the track is worth noting, but Oisin Orr takes the ride and the horse's genuine soft-ground form makes him the most credible hold-up winner if the pace scenario obliges.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner two starts back, Tarmonbarry Kid brings solid recent form to the table, though 73 days off the track is a query and his speed figure of 64 leaves him with ground to make up from stall 12 off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by style — fitted with a tongue tie and blinkers — who has been pushed into a midfield map position purely because the field has too many rear-rangers; David Allan rides a horse who has not won in fifteen soft-ground runs, and his actual finishing position is likely to be further back than the map suggests, tempering his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Mount King has shown little consistency in recent starts, with a ninth and a fourth from his last two outings overshadowing a win four starts back, and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures he is hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old prominent racer fitted with a hood who was beaten fourth last time out and has one win from fifteen attempts at soft or similar going; James Sullivan rides and the step up in trip from seven furlongs to ten-and-a-half is unproven, though her prominent style keeps her competitive if the pace is manageable.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Filey Beach has posted two fourths in his most recent starts and a seventh three runs back, making him hard to fancy despite a win two starts further back; experience over today's trip and going, plus 22 days' freshness, are modest plus points.

runners_data.name: Cobalt Comet
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination — given a hood and running from the rear in his best form — who has been mapped to midfield because the race is saturated with rear-rangers; PJ McDonald is a strong booking but the horse's actual role in running will be nearer the back than shown, and his one soft-ground start produced a place rather than a win, limiting confidence at a higher OR than he has previously won at.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Cobalt Comet faces a stiff task, and a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and going before and did score one start back.

races.paceDynamic: Style Of Life and Glorious Kitty are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, creating a genuinely competitive early gallop over this mile-and-a-half on soft ground at Beverley. The two will push each other along through the first half of the race, meaning the pace should be honest rather than suicidal but enough to stretch the field on a stamina-sapping surface. Sandy Craic and Coolree will attempt to hold prominent positions just off the duelling leaders, while the hold-up horses — Borjina, Good Morning Alex, Regalian, and Tarmonbarry Kid — will be anchored in rear and dependent on the pace not collapsing. This contested front-end shape on soft ground at a course that already favours genuine stayers strongly suits prominent-to-mid-division runners with proven soft-ground stamina, particularly those who can travel close to the pace without burning energy tracking a duel. Mount King and Cobalt Comet are genuine hold-up types that this field's depth forces into midfield positions that are not truly their own, so their actual finishing position will be closer to the rear than the race map implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life and Glorious Kitty push each other hard enough to compromise both their finishes, leaving the race to those who have tracked the pace or swept through from mid-division.
scenarios.body: The contested front-end gallop on soft ground drains the two leaders approaching the home turn, and horses like Sandy Craic and Coolree who have tracked sensibly hit the front with energy remaining. This shape specifically rewards prominent racers with soft-ground credentials who have sat just off a fast pace and can sustain their run up Beverley's home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Style Of Life — proves stronger than the other and establishes a clear lead at halfway, controlling the race from the front.
scenarios.body: Style Of Life, fitted with a tongue tie and proven at this sort of distance, gets the better of Glorious Kitty early and drops into a rhythm that the soft ground does not punish fatally, arriving at the home straight with reserves. A gallop that is honest but not frantic rewards the horse who dictated tempo rather than the chasers who may have been travelling comfortably but find themselves caught cold when the leader refuses to stop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a truly searching gallop that burns off every prominent runner, allowing a hold-up horse to sweep through beaten rivals late.
scenarios.body: Tarmonbarry Kid, the only hold-up type with a genuine soft-ground win on their card, is best placed to benefit if the front-runners commit fully and the mid-division also gets swallowed up. Borjina's excellent Bethell yard form and Kevin Stott's patient riding style make her the other credible option in this shape, though both face the challenge of finding sufficient daylight through a twelve-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits All
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully — perhaps Glorious Kitty drops out of contention early — leaving a single leader setting only a moderate gallop that brings the whole field into contention.
scenarios.body: A steadier tempo negates the stamina advantage of the stayers and turns the race into a sprint from two furlongs out, favouring horses with the highest top-speed rating. Glen Nevis, with strong Beverley form and a tactical Charlie Johnston preparation, and Filey Beach, who has recent winning form over shorter trips, are better suited than most to a race that becomes a sprint test rather than a genuine stamina examination.

watchPoints.text: Style Of Life and Glorious Kitty are both confirmed front-runners — if they race against each other aggressively from flag-fall the pace could collapse or burn them both out, fundamentally reshaping the race for everything behind them.

Tarmonbarry Kid is 73 days off the track for the Fahey stable, who typically have runners fit to run; watch the market for any significant move that would suggest stable confidence despite the layoff.

Mount King and Cobalt Comet are both true hold-up horses mapping into midfield on paper — if they race genuinely wide or further back than shown, any scenario requiring them to be positioned close to the pace will not materialise as drawn.

The soft ground at Beverley has been consistent throughout the card today across all distances and times, so conditions are reliable and unlikely to ease further; stamina and soft-ground experience are the primary filters in this mile-and-a-half heat.

Borjina's trainer Edward Bethell is in strong strike-rate form over the last 14 days (7/29), which is worth tracking against a hold-up horse whose soft-ground stamina at this trip is genuinely untested.
